name: Chlamydia felis (feline conjunctivitis)
short_description: An obligate intracellular bacterium with no free-living form at all: it exists only as a tiny, tough, infectious elementary body (EB, ~0.2-0.3 µm) or as a larger, fragile, dividing reticulate body (RB, ~0.5-1 µm) growing inside a host-cell inclusion. The two-form cycle IS the subject — no other microbe in this atlas has this shape. Infects the conjunctiva of cats above all, causing weeping, gummed-up eyes; NOT the same species as C. trachomatis (human STI/trachoma agent) even though it shares the same genus-level biology.

textbook.1: ⚠️ PARTIAL — EB/RB size-density contrast excellent (verified by magnified crop: many small dense maroon dots vs. fewer, larger, pale mottled circles, some mid-division), all particles correctly confined inside the one coral inclusion outline, free EBs correctly shown extracellular. BUT the host nucleus rendered as two overlapping circles (a glitch reading as either a double nucleus or an odd sphere-highlight artifact) and its boundary line visually fused with the inclusion's own boundary, making 'host nucleus' and 'inclusion membrane' hard to anchor as two distinct structures. Fix-prompt: nucleus must be one single solid disc with one outline, fully separated from the inclusion by a gap of ordinary cytoplasm colour.
textbook.2: ⚠️ PARTIAL — nucleus fix worked perfectly (single solid indigo disc, own clean outline, clearly separated from the inclusion). BUT four pale lilac RB-like circles now appear OUTSIDE the inclusion's coral boundary, floating directly in the cytoplasm — a new regression violating 'every EB and RB sits strictly inside the inclusion.' Fix-prompt: explicit 'zero exceptions' instruction that the cytoplasm outside the inclusion must contain no round particles of either kind.
textbook.3: ✅ PASS (gemini-2.5-flash-image) — verified by magnified crop: nucleus is one clean solid disc, fully separated from the inclusion by a cytoplasm gap, its own distinct outline; ALL EBs (small dense maroon dot clusters) and ALL RBs (larger, pale, mottled-texture circles, 2-3x an EB's diameter, two shown mid-division as a pinched figure-eight) sit strictly inside the single coral inclusion outline, none loose in the cytoplasm; three free EBs shown outside the cell near the teal membrane, illustrating attachment; no flagella, no baked-in text (checked at 2x crop). Anchor pixel-sampling after SVG build confirmed elementary_body lands on a dark dot (RGB ~58,21,25), reticulate_body on a pale circle (~222,205,228), inclusion_membrane on the coral line (~242,164,147), host_nucleus on the indigo fill (~137,124,154), host_membrane on the teal ring (~94,148,147).

sem.1: ✅ PASS — freeze-fracture-style false-color SEM (a deliberate compositional choice: SEM is a surface-only technique, so the only truthful way to show BOTH developmental forms together in this modality is a fractured host cell exposing the inclusion cavity's interior surface, an established real EM technique). Verified by magnified crop: many small, densely-packed, matte deep-maroon EBs with true 3D surface relief vs. fewer, clearly larger, pale lilac-white RBs with a softer quilted/pitted surface texture and a visible central pinch/slit on several (mid-division read as a fracture cross-section); intact surrounding cell surface in warm neutral tan false-colour; no flagella, no baked-in text. Accepted on attempt 1, no re-render needed.

3d.1: ✅ PASS — verified by magnified crop: single solid indigo-violet nucleus, cleanly separated from the inclusion by a cytoplasm gap, gently dented on the side facing the inclusion; single translucent glassy inclusion sphere containing many small solid matte maroon EBs and several clearly larger, paler, softer/glowing lilac RBs (2-3x diameter), two shown mid-division as a pinched dumbbell; three free EBs float near the outer teal membrane outside the cell, one touching it (attachment); natural biological tones throughout (maroon/lilac/peach/teal/indigo), not neon, not near-monochrome; no flagella, no baked-in text. Accepted on attempt 1, no re-render needed. Anchor pixel-sampling confirmed all 5 label points land on the intended structures.

watercolor.1: ❌ FAIL — RBs rendered mostly as hollow/empty outline circles (transparent interior, reading as vacuoles rather than solid dividing bodies) instead of solid pale-lilac washes; the inclusion's outline was fragmented into a wavy, multi-lobed amoeba-like shape rather than one clean boundary, making it ambiguous whether one or several inclusions were being shown; size contrast between some 'RB' circles and EB dots was too weak. Fix-prompt: RBs must be fully filled with solid lilac wash (never hollow), and the inclusion must be exactly one smooth continuous outline.
watercolor.2: ❌ FAIL — RB fill and colour fixed (solid pale lilac), but the single-inclusion instruction was over-applied at the wrong scale: the model drew FOUR separate small single-particle 'inclusions' scattered through the cytoplasm (each its own coral-outlined mini-compartment holding one or two particles) plus loose EBs scattered directly in the cytoplasm outside any boundary — a new regression against 'exactly one inclusion holding everything.' Two bad results in a row on this style → escalated to gemini-3-pro-image per the 2-bad-results rule, with an explicit 'EXACTLY ONE inclusion, not two/three/four, holding ALL particles together' instruction.
watercolor.3: ✅ PASS (gemini-3-pro-image) — verified by magnified crop: exactly one smooth oval coral-outlined inclusion holding every EB and RB together in one packed cluster; EBs are small, solid, fully-filled deep-maroon dots; RBs are clearly larger (2-3x), solid pale-lilac-filled circles with only a soft outline, two shown mid-division as a pinched figure-eight; the host nucleus is one solid indigo-blue kidney-bean shape, visibly dented on the side facing the inclusion, fully separated from it; three free EBs sit just outside the cell's teal outline; warm aged paper fills the frame edge-to-edge with a soft wash halo, no mat/frame/border/sheet-on-surface look; no baked-in text. Anchor pixel-sampling after SVG build confirmed all 5 label points land on the intended structures (elementary_body on a dark dot ~131,54,70; reticulate_body on a pale-lilac fill ~205,178,199; inclusion_membrane on the coral line ~244,164,137; host_nucleus on the indigo fill ~122,118,169; host_membrane on the teal ring ~138,175,168).

reference: ✅ PASS, WITH A RECORDED SPECIES COMPROMISE — TEM crop of Fig. 6A (HeLa-cell panel) from Hovhannisyan et al. 2024, PLOS Pathogens, CC BY 4.0. Confirmed by direct visual inspection: one infected cell, one large round inclusion packed with ~100 small, uniformly dark, electron-dense particles (EBs) and several markedly larger, paler, more open-textured particles (RBs); the original authors' own blue/yellow arrowheads (confirmed against the figure legend: blue=EB, yellow=RB) independently corroborate this reading and match our own colour convention. COMPROMISE, recorded not smoothed over: this shows Chlamydia trachomatis, not Chlamydia felis — no freely-licensed C. felis-specific micrograph exists anywhere searched (Wikimedia Commons, CDC PHIL, NIAID Flickr, PLOS/PMC literature); the developmental-form morphology shown is genus-level biology common to both species, and this is disclosed explicitly in render.md §2, not presented as if it were C. felis. A second candidate (NIAID 'Correlative Light and Electron Micrograph of Infected HeLa Cells', CC BY 2.0) was rejected for being a 500x250px 5-panel composite, far too small to isolate a clean crop from — avoiding the 'lores variant returns 200 first' trap. Native crop 535x516px, upscaled ~2.0x to the 1080x1080 master (noted explicitly, not native high-resolution). The original's own scale bar (plain white bar, 2 µm, no baked-in digits) and the two colour arrowheads were left in place deliberately rather than run through edit_image.py, because (a) they corroborate rather than conflict with our labelling, (b) the scale bar carries no baked-in text, and (c) this reference photo is not used as an SVG label base in this pipeline.
